issues.where: Header 'Verdict: Could not run' and Summary point 3
issues.problem: For the AFDB part, the verdict comes from a local permission refusal, not from the published materials. 2,915 of the 3,200 inputs (91%) are on disk and verified. The run_all.sh job is small in light mode: default plus fast over 160 clusters is about 700 s of single-thread CPU at the authors' EPYC timings, so a few minutes on 4 processes. Under the README scale, 'Could not run' covers data that is gone, broken code or too little hardware. A run that is blocked locally and can be unblocked is none of those. As written, the one-line verdict suggests the paper cannot be checked at all, when only HOMSTRAD truly cannot be.

issues.where: Results, paragraph after the input-checks table ('the complete subset is not representative of the full set')
issues.problem: The numbers 0.6219 and 0.6285 are right (I recomputed them), but the conclusion goes further than the data. A 32-cluster sample has an SEM of about 0.13/sqrt(32) = 0.023, so a gap of +0.017 or +0.021 is under 1 SEM. Most of the gap comes from domain imbalance: complete clusters split 7/7/10/8, and the 8 complete 4-domain clusters average 0.656 against 0.572 for all 40. The paragraph also misses the main use of these 32 clusters. They have the authors' exact inputs (same sequences, so coordinates are the only open question), so a per-cluster comparison against afdb_scores.tsv is the strongest test available, whatever their mean.
issues.fix: Reword: 'Over the 32 complete clusters (7/7/10/8 by domain count) the authors' mean LDDT is 0.6219 (FoldMason) and 0.6285 (Fast), within about 1 SEM of the 160-cluster means. The subset mean is not comparable to C5/C6 because the domain mix differs. A later run should compare these 32 clusters one by one with the authors' values, where a deterministic tool on unchanged inputs should match closely.'
